newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale considers emergency harvest funds.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale considers emergency harvest funds.

text.p: Canada Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale is considering approving emergency funds for waterlogged farmers in Alberta who have weather toughened, damp or as yet unharvested grain, the minister's spokesman said.
"He's aware of the problem, but by legislation he can't do anything until November 15," Goodale spokesman Vern Greenshields said.
But Greenshields said Goodale is "keeping an eye on how much grain is still standing and he's hoping, very quickly after the 15th, to make a decision."
Alberta Agriculture Minister Walter Paszkowski on Tuesday asked Goodale for funds for north and central Alberta.

"Farmers in central and northern Alberta had excessive rain and cold weather since early September. These conditions intensified with heavy snowfalls in late October. As a result, a significant number of farmers have unharvested grain in the fields and many have damp or tough grain in on-farm storage," Paszkowski said in a letter to Goodale.
The Canadian Wheat Board on October 25 also called on Goodale to offer funds to aid farmers with unthreshed, tough and damp grain.
"We're hoping elevator managers will have the forms by late November," CWB spokeswoman Rhea Yates said.
Goodale could invoke the Prairie Grain Advance Payments Act which applies to wheat and barley grown in the CWB's jurisdiction.
The Act would allow payments of up to C$15,000 a farmer for unharvested grain and C$3,000 a farmer to dry grain.
The emergency measure was last invoked in 1993, CWB's Yates said.

Northeast Alberta reported 95 percent of crops in the bin overall. The Athabasca district harvested 70 to 75 percent of crops and Evansburg had 85 to 90 percent in the bin, Alberta Agriculture said in a report for the week ended November 4.

Northeast Alberta reported 85 to 90 percent of crops in the bin in the Bonnyville district, 60 to 90 percent in Lac La Biche district, 70 to 75 percent in St. Paul district and 90 percent in the Vermillion district, Alberta Agriculture said.
The Peace River Valley saw little harvest progress in the past week with 70 to 75 percent of the crop harvested overall. The southwest harvested 25 to 55 percent of crops.
